title: Upstream cannot fork: container PID limit survives restart
root_causes: The harness sets edge-victim-app PidsLimit=3. Kernel cgroup process limits can reject new tasks with EAGAIN; restarting retains container settings. Confirm this hypothesis with live evidence.

checks.purpose: Look for fork/EAGAIN, not OOM; also collect docker_ps and health.
cgroup v2: small limit/reached limit/max events. Exec may itself fail at the PID limit; failure alone proves no cause.

checks.command: search_runbooks {"query":"upstream fork Resource temporarily unavailable pids limit"}
checks.purpose: Correlate logs/limits; no files or no exec means escalate for operator inspect, not invent a value.

remediation.action: After confirmed PID exhaustion, docker_restart {"name":"edge-victim-app"} once, then check_health {}; restart preserves PidsLimit.
If the same confirmed fault and /api/ failure persist after target restart, recreate_stack {"name":"edge-victim-app","replace":true} from approved stateless definition; check_health {}.

OPERATOR ONLY alternative (not an agent tool): docker inspect --format "{{.HostConfig.PidsLimit}}" edge-victim-app; record the value, then docker update --pids-limit <approved-known-good-limit> edge-victim-app and docker restart edge-victim-app. Never guess a limit or remove limits globally.

rollback: For operator limit changes, record the previous and approved known-good limits before changing. If needed restore ONLY a previously healthy limit: docker update --pids-limit <saved-healthy-limit> edge-victim-app; docker restart edge-victim-app. Do not restore the injected limit 3.

Container replacement has no automatic undo of its old writable layer. Before replacement preserve required data/evidence; if the replacement regresses, stop and have the operator restore the approved deployment definition/backup.
verify: check_health {}: require / = 200 AND /api/ = 200; otherwise unresolved, never infer success from a tool response.
docker_ps {}: target stays Up; repeat health after a short observation interval and inspect fresh target logs.
docker_exec {"name":"edge-victim-app","cmd":"cat /sys/fs/cgroup/pids.max /sys/fs/cgroup/pids.current"}: approved PID budget and spare capacity; no new fork errors.
safety: These are failed or uncompleted experiments, not verified repair successes. TIMEOUT records lack final health; some FAIL records also show gateway/compaction errors. Knowledge deficiency is not established.

title: Frontend worker_connections exhausted in image-owned nginx.conf
root_causes: The harness changes edge-victim /etc/nginx/nginx.conf worker_connections from 1024 to 2 in its writable layer. Connections include proxy upstream connections. Confirm the file and log evidence; this is separate from the host-mounted site config.

checks.purpose: Look for worker_connections are not enough and layer-change evidence for /etc/nginx/nginx.conf.
Read events.worker_connections and effective configuration. nginx -t alone can pass this semantic fault.
Confirm backend is healthy; collect docker_ps/health before changing frontend.

remediation.action: With confirmed front limit corruption and healthy backend, docker_restart {"name":"edge-victim"} once; then check_health {}.
If still failing AND actual layer evidence shows altered /etc/nginx/nginx.conf outside conf.d, recreate_stack {"name":"edge-victim","replace":true} under reviewer; check_health {}.

OPERATOR ONLY single-file recovery alternative: preserve the current nginx.conf with docker cp edge-victim:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf <approved-backup-file>; docker cp <validated-known-good-nginx.conf> edge-victim:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf; docker exec edge-victim nginx -t; only after validation, docker restart edge-victim. File must match this image/config layout.

rollback: For single-file recovery, restore the saved file ONLY if it was previously healthy: docker cp <saved-healthy-nginx.conf> edge-victim:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf; docker exec edge-victim nginx -t; docker restart edge-victim. Do not restore the injected worker_connections=2.

Replacement cannot undo its old writable layer automatically. Preserve needed data first; if the new container regresses, escalate with logs and restore the approved image/definition rather than repeating rebuilds.

title: Backend Nginx syntax corruption; target its own config, not frontend
symptoms: unexpected end of file expecting semicolon
root_causes: The harness removes a semicolon in edge-victim-app /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf. This is the backend writable layer, not edge-victim host-mounted config. Stopped containers cannot run docker_exec.

checks.purpose: Require backend nginx [emerg] with file/line; collect docker_ps and health.
Distinguish backend exited/restarting from healthy frontend; never rewrite frontend to fix backend syntax.

checks.command: search_runbooks {"query":"edge-victim-app nginx emerg syntax default.conf backend exited"}
checks.purpose: If running, docker_exec nginx -t on edge-victim-app; read_config/restore_config target frontend only.

remediation.action: For confirmed backend syntax crash, docker_start {"name":"edge-victim-app"} if stopped (docker_restart if running); collect fresh backend logs and check_health {}.
If backend still has the same own-layer syntax failure after target start/restart and /api/ fails, recreate_stack {"name":"edge-victim-app","replace":true} under reviewer; check_health {}.

OPERATOR ONLY single-file recovery alternative, after saving a copy: docker cp edge-victim-app:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf <approved-backup-file>; docker cp <validated-backend-default.conf> edge-victim-app:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf; docker start edge-victim-app. Once running, docker exec edge-victim-app nginx -t and check both health URLs. Never copy the frontend site config into the backend.

rollback: If operator single-file recovery regresses, restore ONLY a saved known-good backend file: docker cp <saved-healthy-backend-default.conf> edge-victim-app:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf; docker restart edge-victim-app. Do not restore the injected invalid file.

Replacement has no automatic writable-layer undo. Preserve required state first; if it fails, escalate with the backend logs and restore the approved backend definition/backup. If a frontend was changed in this incident, separately use restore_config {"source":"previous"} only when that saved frontend config was confirmed healthy, then docker_restart {"name":"edge-victim"} and check_health.
